update-story-log.description: Summarizes the latest episode and prepends it to the StoryLog.md file.
steps: Read the most recent episode file from the 'Campaign/Episodes/' directory.
Summarize the key events from the notes.
Format the summary using the 'Story Log Entry Template'.
Prepend the formatted summary to the 'Campaign/StoryLog.md' file, ensuring the new entry is at the top.
Identify any locations or characters mentioned in the summary.
For each location, append a summary of the key events to the 'Role in Campaign' section of the corresponding location file.
For each character, append a summary of the key events to the 'Role in Campaign' section of the corresponding character file.
For each faction, append a summary of the key events to the 'Role in Campaign' section of the corresponding faction file.
Identify all content used (NPCs, locations, items, etc.) and add them as a linked list under the '### Content Used' section in the new StoryLog.md entry.
Create the 'Campaign/Quest Hooks/Complete/' directory if it does not exist.
Create the 'Campaign/Puzzles/Complete/' directory if it does not exist.
For each quest hook that was completed, update the 'Status' section of the corresponding quest hook file to 'Completed' and move the file to the 'Campaign/Quest Hooks/Complete/' directory.
For each puzzle that was completed, update the 'Status' section of the corresponding puzzle file to 'Completed' and move the file to the 'Campaign/Puzzles/Complete/' directory.
For each player character, if they had a significant, unique role in the events, append a summary of their contribution to the 'Campaign Notes' section of their character file.
If a quest hook was completed, mark it as '(Completed)' in the location file.
If a puzzle was completed, mark it as '(Completed)' in the location file.

next-episode.description: Generates the next sequential episode file.
steps: Determine the next episode number by checking the existing files in the 'Campaign/Episodes/' directory.
Create a new file named 'E[Next Number].md' in the 'Campaign/Episodes/' directory.
Populate the new file with the 'Episode Template', filling in the episode number and the current date.

create-location.description: Generates a new location file based on a name and type.
steps: Ask the user for the name and type of the location (e.g., city, town, forest, region).
If the location is a dungeon, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Dungeons/' directory.
If the location is a region, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Regions/' directory.
Otherwise, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Settlements/' directory.
Populate the new file using the 'Location Template'.
Fill in the name and type, and then generate the rest of the content.
Ask the user if they would like to generate an ASCII map for the location.
If the user agrees, generate a map and add it to the 'Map' section of the location file.

create-npc.description: Generates a new NPC file based on a name and race/class.
steps: Ask the user for the NPC's name, race, class, and alignment.
Create a new file named '[NPC Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Characters/' directory.
Populate the new file using the 'NPC Template'.
Fill in the provided details and generate the rest of the content.

create-dungeon.description: Generates a new dungeon location with puzzles.
steps: Ask the user for the name and type of the dungeon.
Create a new file named '[Dungeon Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Dungeons/' directory.
Populate the file using the 'Location Template', including points of interest and key NPCs.
Generate 1-2 unique puzzles for the dungeon.
Create a new file for each puzzle in the 'Campaign/Puzzles/' directory.
Link the puzzle files from the main dungeon file.
Ask the user if they would like to generate an ASCII map for the dungeon.
If the user agrees, generate a map and add it to the 'Map' section of the dungeon file.

generate-location.description: Generates a new location on-the-fly with minimal input.
steps: Ask the user if they have any key details they would like to provide (e.g., 'a bustling port town with a seedy underbelly', 'a quiet village in a haunted forest').
Generate a name for the location.
Determine the type of location (dungeon, region, or settlement) based on the key details.
If the location is a dungeon, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Dungeons/' directory.
If the location is a region, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Regions/' directory.
Otherwise, create a new file named '[Location Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Settlements/' directory.
Populate the file using the 'Location Template', generating all content based on the user's key details.
Ask the user if they would like to generate an ASCII map for the location.
If the user agrees, generate a map and add it to the 'Map' section of the location file.

generate-npc.description: Generates a new NPC on-the-fly with minimal input.
steps: Ask the user if they have any key details they would like to provide (e.g., 'a gruff blacksmith with a heart of gold', 'a mysterious wizard who lives in a tower').
Generate a name, race, class, and alignment for the NPC.
Create a new file named '[NPC Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Characters/' directory.
Populate the file using the 'NPC Template', generating all content based on the user's key details.

generate-dungeon.description: Generates a new dungeon on-the-fly with minimal input.
steps: Ask the user if they have any key details they would like to provide (e.g., 'a goblin-infested mine', 'a forgotten temple to a dark god').
Generate a name for the dungeon.
Create a new file named '[Dungeon Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Locations/Dungeons/' directory.
Populate the file using the 'Location Template', generating all content, including points of interest, NPCs, and 1-2 unique puzzles.
Create new files for the puzzles in the 'Campaign/Puzzles/' directory and link them from the main dungeon file.
Ask the user if they would like to generate an ASCII map for the dungeon.
If the user agrees, generate a map and add it to the 'Map' section of the dungeon file.

create-religion.description: Generates a new religion file based on a name and type.
steps: Ask the user for the name and type of the religion (e.g., deity, faith, pantheon).
Create a new file named '[Religion Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Religions/' directory.
Populate the new file using the 'Religion Template'.
Fill in the name and type, and then generate the rest of the content.

generate-religion.description: Generates a new religion on-the-fly with minimal input.
steps: Ask the user if they have any key details they would like to provide (e.g., 'a god of courage and self-sacrifice', 'a mysterious cult worshipping shadows').
Generate a name for the religion.
Determine the type of religion (deity, faith, or pantheon) based on the key details.
Create a new file named '[Religion Name].md' in the 'Campaign/Religions/' directory.
Populate the file using the 'Religion Template', generating all content based on the user's key details.

plan-arc.description: Generates a new story arc planning document using the official template.
steps: Ask the user for the name of the story arc (or provide notes to generate one), target player level range, session time estimates (default 3-4 hours unless specified), optional notes file, and desired session count.
Create a new file in 'Campaign/Planning/' prefixed with 'Arc-' and named after the arc (e.g., 'Arc-Fallen Paladin.md').
Populate the new file using the 'Story Arc Template'.
Fill in the provided details and generate a session-by-session breakdown.

create-arc.description: Reads a story arc plan and creates files for major resources using the official templates.
steps: Ask the user to specify which story arc plan to use.
Read the specified markdown file.
Identify all names enclosed in [[Double Brackets]] as major resources.
For each major resource, determine its type (NPC, Location, Faction, etc.).
Check if a file for the resource already exists.
If the file does not exist, create a new file in the appropriate directory.
Populate the new file using the corresponding template (e.g., 'NPC Template' for an NPC).
Fill in the name and any other details available from the planning document.
Update the planning document to convert the [[Resource Name]] to a standard markdown link.

generate-share.description: Generates a player-safe, copy-pastable markdown file version of a file.
steps: Ask the user for the path to the markdown file they want to share.
Read the content of the specified file.
Create a new file with the same name as the original, but with '-Share' appended to the name.
In the new file, remove all markdown links formatted as '[text](link)' and replace them with just the text 'text'.
In the new file, remove any lines that contain only placeholder text in parentheses, such as '(A summary of key story points...)' or '(Copy/paste background blurb...)'.
Inform the user that the new file has been created.
